summary: Per-instance color holder: stores one color locally so many visual inputs can share a single editable source.
description: Color holds a single color value that belongs to this node instance alone, defaulting to '#f1f2f4'. The `value` input sets it (via the editor's color picker or a connection) and `savedValue` (Value) reads it back. While the `saveValue` (Set) signal input is unconnected, values written to `value` apply immediately; once `saveValue` is connected the node latches: incoming values are held pending and only applied when Set fires. Unlike the Boolean/Number/String holders it applies no cast — the value passes through unchanged. Browser-only; not available in cloud functions. `changed` fires only when the stored value actually changes; `stored` fires after every Set trigger.
whenToUse: Use it as a single source of truth for a color used in several places — wire `savedValue` to every `backgroundColor`, `color` or border input that should match, and edit one node to restyle them all. For project-wide theming prefer style colors; a String can also drive color inputs (any CSS color string casts), but Color gives you the picker.

ports.value: Color value input with the editor's color picker. Applies immediately while Value is ticked under Run On Value Change (the default); untick it to hold the value until Set fires.
ports.saveValue: Signal; applies the most recently received `value`, then reports Done or Unchanged.
ports.savedValue: Color level with the currently stored color; fan it out to any number of visual color inputs.
ports.changed: Signal; fires only when the stored value actually changes.
ports.done: Signal; a Set stored a value the Variable was not already holding.
ports.unchanged: Signal; a Set stored the value it already held, so nothing changed. ⚠️ With Value left ticked under Run On Value Change this is the common case, because Value has already stored by the time Set fires — untick it if you want Set to be the only thing that writes.
ports.completed: Signal; fires after every Set, whatever the outcome. This is what the old `Stored` port meant, and it replaces it. ⚠️ A Value that wrote straight through reports nothing at all — that is not an invocation of Set.

patterns: One accent color: `savedValue` → several nodes' `backgroundColor`/`color` inputs, so a design tweak is one edit.
Runtime theme switch: a Switch or States feeds `value`, and every connected visual updates together.
